events.title: The Word Becomes Flesh
events.description: John introduces the divine Word as the source of creation, life, and light, then identifies his coming into human life with Jesus Christ. The incarnate Son reveals the unseen God and brings grace and truth.

events.title: John the Baptist Testifies About Jesus
events.description: Priests and Levites question John about his identity and baptism at Bethany across the Jordan. John denies being the Messiah and identifies Jesus as God's Son, whose mission removes sin and brings the Holy Spirit.

events.title: Jesus Gathers His First Disciples
events.description: Two of John's disciples follow Jesus, and Andrew brings his brother Simon, whom Jesus renames Peter. Jesus then calls Philip, who brings Nathanael; Nathanael's encounter leads him to recognize Jesus as Israel's king.

events.title: Jesus Turns Water Into Wine at Cana
events.description: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus directs servants to fill purification jars with water, which becomes wine. This first sign reveals his glory to the disciples, who deepen their trust in him.

events.title: Jesus Clears Commerce From the Temple
events.description: At Passover Jesus drives merchants and money changers from the temple precincts. Challenged for a sign, he points cryptically to the destruction and raising of his body, an image the disciples understand after his resurrection.

events.title: Jesus Teaches Nicodemus at Night
events.description: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and Jewish leader, visits Jesus by night. Jesus teaches him about birth through the Spirit, the Son's heavenly origin and coming exaltation, and God's saving purpose for a world divided by its response to the light.

events.title: Jesus' Disciples Baptize in Judea
events.description: Jesus' disciples baptize in Judea while John continues his work near Salim. When John's followers worry about Jesus' growing audience, John accepts his own diminishing role and renews his witness to the Son's heavenly authority.

events.title: Jesus Speaks With a Samaritan Woman
events.description: Traveling through Samaria, Jesus speaks with a woman at Jacob's well about living water, her life, true worship, and his identity. Her testimony brings people from Sychar, and many come to believe during Jesus' two-day stay.

events.title: Jesus Heals an Official's Son From Afar
events.description: At Cana a royal official pleads for his dying son in Capernaum. Jesus assures him that the child will live, and the recovery at that same hour brings the official and his household to faith.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Disabled Man at Beth-zatha
events.description: During a Jerusalem festival Jesus heals a man who has been disabled for thirty-eight years and tells him to carry his mat. Because the healing occurs on the Sabbath and Jesus describes God as his Father, hostility against him intensifies.

events.title: Jesus Explains the Son's Authority
events.description: Jesus teaches that the Son acts in unity with the Father and has authority to give life, judge, and raise the dead. He appeals to John's witness, his own works, the Father's testimony, and the writings of Moses against those who refuse him.

events.title: Jesus Feeds Five Thousand Near Passover
events.description: Near Passover a large crowd follows Jesus beside the Sea of Galilee. He multiplies five barley loaves and two fish to feed them, but withdraws when they intend to force kingship upon him.

events.title: Jesus Walks Across the Sea
events.description: After dark the disciples row toward Capernaum through rough water. Jesus approaches their boat by walking on the sea, calms their fear, and they reach their destination.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Bread of Life
events.description: The crowd finds Jesus at Capernaum after the feeding. He redirects their pursuit from temporary food to trust in the one sent by God and presents himself as the life-giving bread from heaven, provoking dispute over his claims.

events.title: Many Disciples Turn Away From Jesus
events.description: Many followers reject Jesus' difficult teaching and cease traveling with him. Peter affirms the Twelve's trust in Jesus, while Jesus warns that one among them will betray him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches at the Festival of Booths
events.description: Jesus travels privately to Jerusalem for the Festival of Booths and begins teaching publicly midway through it. Crowds debate his identity, authorities attempt to arrest him, and Jesus defends his Sabbath healing and divine commission.

events.title: Jesus Offers Living Water at the Festival
events.description: On the festival's final day Jesus uses thirst and flowing water to describe the Spirit believers will receive. The declaration divides the crowd, temple police decline to arrest him, and Nicodemus challenges the leaders to grant him a hearing.

events.title: Jesus Refuses to Condemn an Accused Woman
events.description: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman accused of adultery before Jesus as a test. He confronts the accusers with their own sin; they depart, and he releases the woman with a charge to abandon sin.

events.title: Jesus Debates His Opponents About Truth and Abraham
events.description: Teaching in the temple, Jesus presents himself as the world's light and grounds his testimony in the Father who sent him. Debate over freedom, ancestry, and divine sonship escalates until his claim to precede Abraham prompts an attempt to stone him.

events.title: Jesus Gives Sight to a Man Born Blind
events.description: Jesus makes mud and sends a man born blind to wash at Siloam, restoring his sight on the Sabbath. Repeated questioning leads the healed man to defend Jesus and be expelled, after which Jesus finds him and receives his worship.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Good Shepherd
events.description: Using the images of a sheepfold, gate, flock, and shepherd, Jesus contrasts his protective self-giving with thieves and hired hands. His claim to lay down and take up his life again divides his hearers.

events.title: Jesus Faces Threats at the Festival of Dedication
events.description: During winter at the Festival of Dedication, Jesus identifies his works as testimony and describes the unity of his action with the Father. Opponents attempt to stone and arrest him, but he escapes across the Jordan, where many believe.

events.title: Jesus Raises Lazarus From the Dead
events.description: After Lazarus dies at Bethany, Jesus arrives when he has been entombed four days. He comforts Martha and Mary, weeps with the mourners, then calls Lazarus from the tomb alive.

events.title: The Council Plans Jesus' Death
events.description: Lazarus's restoration leads many to believe, while others report it to the Pharisees. Caiaphas persuades the council that Jesus should die for the nation, and Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches.

events.title: Mary Anoints Jesus at Bethany
events.description: Six days before Passover, Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly perfume at a dinner in Bethany. Jesus connects her act with his burial, while the chief priests expand their plot to include Lazarus because his survival draws believers.

events.title: Jesus Enters Jerusalem as a King
events.description: Festival crowds welcome Jesus with palm branches as he enters Jerusalem on a young donkey. Witnesses spread news of Lazarus's raising, and the Pharisees fear the breadth of his appeal.

events.title: Greeks Seek Jesus as His Public Ministry Closes
events.description: Greek worshipers ask to see Jesus, who announces that his glorifying hour has arrived and compares fruitful death to a planted grain. A heavenly voice answers his prayer, and he gives a final public appeal to believe in the light despite widespread resistance.

events.title: Jesus Washes His Disciples' Feet
events.description: During supper before Passover, Jesus washes the disciples' feet despite Peter's objection. He presents his humble service as the pattern they should practice toward one another.

events.title: Jesus Identifies His Betrayer
events.description: Troubled at supper, Jesus announces that one disciple will betray him and gives a morsel to Judas as the identifying sign. Judas departs into the night to carry out the betrayal.

events.title: Jesus Commands Love and Predicts Peter's Denial
events.description: After Judas leaves, Jesus commands the disciples to love one another in the pattern of his own love. Peter promises to follow him at any cost, but Jesus predicts that Peter will deny him three times before morning.

events.title: Jesus Promises the Father's Presence and the Spirit
events.description: Jesus comforts his disciples with the promise of a place with the Father and identifies himself as their way to God. He promises that the Holy Spirit will teach and remind them, and leaves them peace before his departure.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Abiding, Love, and Witness
events.description: Jesus depicts himself as a vine whose branches bear fruit by remaining in him. He calls the disciples friends, commands mutual love, warns of the world's hostility, and commissions them to testify alongside the Spirit.

events.title: Jesus Prepares the Disciples for Sorrow and Joy
events.description: Jesus warns that the disciples will face expulsion and persecution, yet says his departure enables the Spirit's coming. He promises that their approaching grief will turn to joy and encourages them to find peace in his victory.

events.title: Jesus Prays for His Disciples and Future Believers
events.description: Jesus prays that the Father will glorify him as his earthly work reaches completion. He asks protection, holiness, unity, and shared glory for his disciples and for those who will believe through their witness.

events.title: Jesus Is Arrested in the Garden
events.description: Judas leads soldiers and temple police to the garden across the Kidron. Jesus steps forward and submits to arrest while securing the disciples' release, and Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant Malchus.

events.title: Annas Questions Jesus as Peter Denies Him
events.description: Jesus is questioned about his teaching before Annas and then sent bound to Caiaphas. Meanwhile Peter denies association with Jesus three times beside a charcoal fire before the rooster crows.

events.title: Pilate Questions Jesus
events.description: The authorities bring Jesus to Pilate early in the morning and seek a Roman judgment against him. Pilate questions Jesus about kingship and truth, finds no case against him, and offers to release him, but the crowd chooses Barabbas.

events.title: Pilate Sentences Jesus to Crucifixion
events.description: Soldiers flog and mock Jesus with royal dress and a thorny crown. Though Pilate repeatedly presents him as innocent and tries to release him, political pressure from the chief priests leads him to authorize crucifixion.

events.title: Jesus Is Crucified and Dies
events.description: Jesus is crucified at Golgotha between two others under Pilate's inscription naming him king of the Jews. He entrusts his mother to the beloved disciple, dies, and is confirmed dead when a soldier pierces his side.

events.title: Joseph and Nicodemus Bury Jesus
events.description: Joseph of Arimathea receives permission to remove Jesus' body, and Nicodemus brings a large quantity of burial spices. They wrap the body and place it in a nearby new garden tomb before the Sabbath.

events.title: Peter and the Beloved Disciple Find the Tomb Empty
events.description: Before dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene finds the tomb open and alerts Peter and the beloved disciple. They run to the tomb and find the burial cloths without Jesus' body.

events.title: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene
events.description: Mary remains weeping near the empty tomb and initially mistakes the risen Jesus for the gardener. When he addresses her personally, she recognizes him and carries news of the encounter to the disciples.

events.title: Jesus Appears to the Gathered Disciples
events.description: On the evening of the resurrection, Jesus appears among disciples gathered behind locked doors. He shows his wounds, commissions them as the Father sent him, and breathes the Holy Spirit upon them.

events.title: Jesus Appears to Thomas
events.description: Thomas doubts the other disciples' report because he was absent from Jesus' first appearance. A week later Jesus appears again and invites Thomas to examine his wounds, prompting Thomas's confession of faith.

events.title: Jesus Provides a Catch and Breakfast by the Sea
events.description: Seven disciples fish overnight on the Sea of Tiberias without success. At daybreak the risen Jesus directs them to a great catch and serves them bread and fish on the shore.

events.title: Jesus Entrusts His Flock to Peter
events.description: After breakfast Jesus asks Peter three times about his love and entrusts him with care for the community. He foretells Peter's costly death, calls him again to follow, and corrects speculation about the beloved disciple's future.
